Logistics ● Ongoing hourly contract, not a one-off project ● Expected 100 hours per month. L16 Summarizing and Modeling with the Analytics Pane Lab: Add totals, an average line with a distribution band, a parameter-driven reference line, trend models, a customized forecast and MODEL_QUANTILE. L17 Building and Formatting Dashboards Lab: Assemble the Regional Performance dashboard in containers, format it with padding, palette and annotations, and build the phone layout. description: ## Senior Research & Strategy Analyst / Right Hand to Founder & CEO I’m building **Plain Sight Strategy**, a boutique research, insights and strategy consultancy focused primarily on U.S.-based clients. I’ve spent nearly 20 years working inside major companies, leading market research, consumer insights and strategy teams and partnering with businesses across media, entertainment, technology and other industries. Over those years, I’ve worked with a lot of research vendors. I also spent a lot of time wishing the vendor I really needed existed. Someone who didn’t just take the brief and disappear. Someone who understood the business question behind the research request. Someone who could challenge the methodology when necessary, connect the dots across different sources of information, understand the audience in context, and come back with something more useful than a deck full of findings. **Plain Sight is the company I always wished I had on the other side of the table.** Now I’m building it. And I’m looking for someone who could eventually become my **right hand in that process**. This person will report directly to me, the Founder & CEO, and work closely with me across client discovery, scoping, research design, analysis, strategy and delivery. Initially, this will be a freelance/contract role as client engagements come in. But I am not looking for someone I have to replace every time a project ends. For the right person, I want this relationship to grow with the business. You would be coming in early enough to help shape how we work, how we approach client problems, how we deliver research and insights, and ultimately what kind of consultancy Plain Sight becomes. ### What I need I need a strong second set of eyes and ears. Someone I can bring onto a prospective client call who is listening beyond the words being said. Someone who can hear a client say, “We need a survey,” and already be thinking: *Do they?* *What are they actually trying to understand?* *What decision are they trying to make?* *What information do they already have?* *What are we missing?* *Is research even the first thing they need?* That is the level of thinking I’m looking for. Sometimes a client may think they need a survey when they really need existing-data analysis. They may ask for “market research” when the underlying issue is positioning, audience strategy, customer understanding, segmentation, messaging, market opportunity, or something else entirely. I need someone who can help me diagnose that quickly and thoughtfully. After those conversations, you may help me: * Debrief client meetings and identify the real business or research question * Recommend the appropriate research or strategy approach * Develop project scopes, methodologies, timelines and deliverables * Think through sample requirements, audiences and research design * Draft surveys, screeners, discussion guides and other research materials * Analyze quantitative and qualitative research * Review crosstabs, datasets and open-ended responses * Identify patterns and surface the insights that actually matter * Pressure-test findings and recommendations * Build the story behind the data * Help develop client presentations and reports * Track project details and keep work moving between meetings * Review work from other freelancers, panel providers and specialist vendors when additional support is brought in I will remain the primary client lead and final decision-maker. But I do not want someone who simply waits for instructions. I want someone who will come to me and say: “I noticed something on that call.” “I think there’s another issue underneath what they’re asking us.” “I don’t think the data supports that conclusion.” “We should look at this before we make the recommendation.” “Something about this doesn’t make sense.” That kind of curiosity and judgment is exactly what I want around me. ### Deep understanding of the U.S. market is required Plain Sight’s clients will primarily be **U.S.-based**, and research, insights and strategy are part of the core of what we do. That means understanding the U.S. market cannot simply be something listed on your résumé. You need to understand the context behind the numbers. You should be comfortable thinking about: * U.S. consumer behavior and market dynamics * Demographic and generational differences * Multicultural audiences and differences in lived experience * Regional differences across the U.S. * Media, entertainment, brands and the broader marketing environment * U.S.-based sampling and research considerations * How culture, economics and social context can change the way findings should be interpreted You do not necessarily need to live in the United States. You **do** need meaningful professional experience working with U.S. clients, U.S. audiences and U.S.-based research. This is not a role where someone can learn the U.S. market as they go. ### The person I’m looking for You likely have a background in some combination of: * Market research * Consumer or audience insights * Customer insights * Research consulting * Marketing strategy * Business strategy * Media or entertainment research * Brand research and strategy You should be comfortable with both **quantitative and qualitative research**. You do not have to personally execute every advanced methodology. Part of being good at this job is knowing what you know, what you don’t know, and when we need to bring in another specialist. Strong analytical ability matters. But I am not looking for someone whose contribution ends with producing tables and charts. I care much more about whether you naturally ask: **So what?** **Why does this matter?** **What does this mean for the business?** **What should the client do differently because we learned this?** Strong candidates will have several years of professional market research, insights or strategy experience; significant experience with U.S.-based clients or audiences; strong research design and methodology knowledge; excellent critical thinking; strong PowerPoint and storytelling skills; good judgment with confidential information; and the confidence to respectfully challenge my thinking when appropriate. Experience with tools such as Excel, SPSS, R, Qualtrics or similar platforms is helpful. You do not need to be an expert in every tool. ### Client exposure This is not a role where you disappear behind the scenes and only send me analysis. I want this person in the room. Depending on the engagement, you may join discovery calls, scope conversations, working sessions, research readouts and other client meetings. At first, your role will primarily be to listen closely, capture what matters, identify gaps and support me in shaping the engagement. As trust develops, I expect the right person to become increasingly comfortable contributing directly to those conversations. Because our clients will primarily be U.S.-based, you should have reasonable availability during **U.S. Eastern Time business hours** for scheduled meetings. ### Reporting structure You will report directly to me, the Founder & CEO. I will set the overall client strategy, approve scopes and recommendations, and remain the primary owner of the client relationship. At the same time, I want someone whose perspective I respect enough to ask: **“What am I missing?”** This role will have meaningful responsibility, access and influence, but the reporting structure needs to be comfortable for you. I am not looking for a co-founder or equal business partner. I am looking for a strong, trusted person who can become the right hand to the Founder/CEO as the company grows. ### Why this could become something bigger This is probably the most important thing to understand about the opportunity. I’m not building Plain Sight because I wanted to become an independent freelancer. I’m building a company. My goal is to take what I learned from nearly two decades working inside large organizations — what worked, what didn’t, what clients actually need from research partners, and where traditional vendors consistently fell short — and build something better. I want Plain Sight to be the consultancy clients call when the problem is still messy. When they know something is happening with their customers or audience but don’t yet know how to articulate it. When they have plenty of data but not enough clarity. When they need someone who can move comfortably between research, insights, strategy and the business decision that ultimately needs to be made. The person I hire for this role would be joining very early in that journey. There will be ambiguity. There will be things we build for the first time. There will probably be processes we create, change and improve as the company grows. For the right person, that is the exciting part. If you want a tightly defined role inside an established organization where every process already exists, this probably will not be the right fit. If the idea of helping build a boutique consultancy from its early stages — and potentially growing into a significant role within it — genuinely excites you, I’d like to hear from you. To apply Please don’t send a generic proposal or simply repeat your résumé. I’m much more interested in understanding how you’ve actually worked and how you think. Please answer these three questions using real examples from your experience rather than hypothetical answers. You may anonymize clients or companies where necessary. 1. Tell me about one U.S.-based research, insights or strategy project that best represents the kind of work you’re good at. What was the business problem, what did you personally own, and what did the client or business ultimately do differently because of the work? 2. Tell me about a time when a client or senior stakeholder came to you asking for one thing, but you realized the real problem was something different. What tipped you off? What did you do with that realization? And what did the work ultimately become? 3. Think about the best working relationship you’ve had with a direct manager or senior leader. What made the two of you work so well together? Now tell me one thing that can make it difficult for you to work well with a leader. There isn't a perfect answer to this question. I'm interested in understanding how you work and whether the way you operate will fit what I'm building. If possible, please also attach one relevant work sample that you personally contributed to and briefly explain what portion of it was yours. I care much more about how you think, how you work and the judgment you bring than how polished your Upwork profile looks.
